title: Pixie Dust Technologies “kikippa” Speaker Ranked First on the Rakuten Sound Bar Ranking
summary: Pixie Dust Technologies' "kikippa" speaker achieved the top position on the Rakuten Sound Bar Ranking in February 2024. The speaker, which processes and outputs "gamma wave sound" with 40Hz modulation, is widely distributed on major e-commerce platforms. This recognition on Rakuten, a prominent Japanese online marketplace, significantly boosts the product's visibility and market acceptance.

title: Esports Investing: Opportunities & Strategies
summary: Esports is a rapidly growing industry with significant investment opportunities despite its relative newness. Investors can gain exposure through companies involved in game development, streaming platforms, hardware/software manufacturing, or through dedicated esports ETFs. While growth prospects are strong, investors should be prepared for volatility and perform thorough due diligence.

title: Astec harmonizes BMH, Con-E-Co, RexCon offerings across dealer base
summary: Effective this month, Astec Industries dealers will offer the complete BMH, Con-E-Co, and RexCon concrete equipment line, including portable and stationary plant series, as well as batching components and accessories. This initiative aims to streamline sales and service, providing a comprehensive selection through a single channel to meet diverse plant or site needs. Company executives emphasize that this expansion offers customers more choice, better efficiency, and strengthens their connection with the company by providing a one-stop shop for concrete batching solutions.

title: EQT Corp. (EQT) to Acquire Avetta from WCAS
summary: EQT Private Equity's EQT X fund has agreed to acquire Avetta, a global leader in supply chain risk management software, from Welsh, Carson, Anderson & Stowe (WCAS). EQT plans to support Avetta's continued growth through product innovation, AI adoption, and global expansion. The transaction is subject to regulatory approvals and financial terms were not disclosed.

title: F5 Networks (FFIV) Appoints Kunal Anand as Chief Technology Officer
summary: F5, Inc. announced the appointment of Kunal Anand as Executive Vice President and Chief Technology Officer (CTO), alongside Lyra Schramm as Executive Vice President and Chief People Officer (CPO). Anand will be responsible for F5's technology vision, leveraging his expertise in cybersecurity and data to accelerate the company's leadership in application and API security. Schramm will focus on driving people initiatives and fostering an innovative workplace culture.

title: Should Invesco S&P 500 Revenue ETF (RWL) Be on Your Investing Radar?
summary: This article evaluates the Invesco S&P 500 Revenue ETF (RWL), a passively managed large-cap value ETF with over $2.98 billion in assets. The article also discusses its sector allocation, top holdings like Walmart and Amazon, and positions it as a medium-risk option with a "Hold" rating from Zacks, comparing it to other value ETFs.

title: Introducing the Newest Innovation from Clorox Brands
summary: Clorox Brands has introduced a host of new products across their portfolio despite a cyberattack in August 2023. These innovations cater to consumer trends such as self-care, sustainability, and experiential flavors, with products ranging from refillable Brita filters and new Burt's Bees lip care to concentrated Pine-Sol formulas and an array of new Hidden Valley Ranch dressings. The new offerings aim to enhance existing platforms and meet diverse consumer needs in home care, wellness, and food.

summary: The VanEck Retail ETF (RTH), which invests in 25 prominent retailers, has outperformed its benchmark over the last six months. title: Why The Honest Company believes their customers are 'brilliant'
summary: Carla Vernón, CEO of The Honest Company, emphasizes transparency and treating customers as "brilliant" by informing them of price changes and offering trustworthy products. The company, co-founded by Jessica Alba, saw a 10% revenue increase in Q4 2023, attributing success to its "Honest Standard" and commitment to clean, sustainably designed personal-care items. Vernón discusses her role as a female Afro-Latina CEO, her high standards, and the company's strategic focus on data-driven decisions and financial discipline to grow responsibly and meet consumer needs.

title: Spotify to raise prices of plans in some markets, Bloomberg News reports
summary: Spotify is reportedly planning to increase its subscription prices by $1 to $2 per month in several markets, including the UK, Australia, and Pakistan, by the end of April. Prices in the United States are expected to rise later in the year, alongside the introduction of a new basic tier offering music and podcasts but no audiobooks. This move aims to boost profitability for the company, which forecasts strong subscriber growth and is diversifying its offerings beyond music.

title: Costco offering members access to weight-loss programs including medication
summary: Costco Wholesale is expanding its partnership with online healthcare provider Sesame to offer its members access to weight-loss programs, including prescriptions for drugs like Ozempic and Wegovy. Members can subscribe to Sesame's weight-loss program for a discounted rate, with clinicians providing guidance on diet and lifestyle, and potentially prescribing medication, though the subscription does not cover medication costs. This move follows similar healthcare service offerings from other major retailers like Amazon and Walmart, as demand for GLP-1 protagonist drugs continues to surge.

title: Kristen Wiig's Target Lady to tout Target Circle Week sale, which runs April 7-13
summary: Target is launching its first-ever Target Circle Week from April 7-13, coinciding with the debut of a revamped loyalty program and the return of Kristen Wiig's "Target Lady" in a new advertising campaign. The sale offers significant discounts across various categories, including 40% off floorcare and 30% off spring apparel and home goods. Target is also introducing Target Circle 360, a paid membership for free same-day delivery, and a new Target Circle Card offering 5% off purchases and other benefits.

title: Alger Launches 2 Transparent Actively Managed ETFs
summary: Fred Alger Management has launched two new transparent actively managed ETFs: the Alger AI Enablers & Adopters ETF (ALAI) and the Alger Concentrated Equity ETF (CNEQ). ALAI focuses on companies involved with artificial intelligence, while CNEQ invests in large-cap growth companies, with a significant allocation to technology. These additions bring Alger's ETF family to five funds, building on their earlier entry into the ETF market in 2021.

summary: This article details the holdings of the Alger Concentrated Equity ETF (CNEQ), which was created on April 5, 2024. title: Uber Freight hires CH Robinson, Amazon veterans
summary: Uber Freight has expanded its leadership team by hiring two seasoned transportation veterans: Dan Annunziata as head of commercial and Hany Elkordy as head of logistics and last mile solutions. Annunziata, formerly a VP at C.H. Robinson, will focus on unifying commercial and sales operations, while Elkordy, with experience from Amazon, Walmart, and Chewy, will lead parcel modality enhancements. These appointments follow other strategic hires as Uber Freight continues to enhance its competitive edge in the brokerage space.

title: Target rolls out Target Circle 360 paid membership
summary: Target has officially launched its new paid membership program, Target Circle 360, costing $99 annually. This program offers same-day delivery with Shipt on orders over $35, an extended return window of 30 days, and free two-day shipping. Target is running a promotional offer of $49 for the first year if customers sign up by May 18, with this price also applying to Target Circle Card holders for more than just the first year.

title: Apple Signs Deal For AI Training Data from Image Service Shutterstock
summary: Apple has signed a deal worth between $25 million and $50 million with Shutterstock to access its vast archive of images, video, and music for training AI systems. This move indicates Apple's strategic intent to develop its own AI models, rather than relying solely on existing solutions. The deal highlights Apple's characteristic approach to adhere to rules and protect user privacy, contrasting with some competitors' controversial methods of data acquisition.

summary: Capital One's proposed $35.3 billion merger with Discover was the largest tech-related M&A deal globally in Q1, contributing to a significant jump in overall tech-related deal value to $183.7 billion. This increase reflects growing corporate confidence amid improving macroeconomic conditions, despite a decrease in the total number of deals. The article also discusses contributing factors like the drive for growth and AI advancements, as well as headwinds such as high interest rates, geopolitical uncertainty, and increased antitrust scrutiny.

title: Fidelity Hedged Equity ETF Holdings
summary: The Fidelity Hedged Equity ETF (FHEQ), established on April 9, 2024, is an actively managed ETF focusing on large-cap equity. title: Google introduces new Arm-based AI chip for data centers
summary: Google has announced its new custom-designed Arm-based AI chips, called Axion Processors, for data centers. These processors are designed to offer better performance and energy efficiency compared to x86 chips and general-purpose Arm chips. The Axion Processors will be available to Google Cloud customers later this year and are already in use in some of Google's own services.

title: As Amazon's stock hovers near a record, its bonds are also looking attractive
summary: Amazon's stock is nearing an all-time high, but its corporate bonds are also presenting an attractive opportunity due to increased yields. title: Cereal giant Post is bringing a distribution center to North Texas
summary: Post Consumer Brands, a division of Post Holdings Inc. (NYSE: POST), known for cereals like Fruity Pebbles and Honeycomb, is establishing a 1.1 million-square-foot distribution center in Wilmer, near Dallas. This move follows the company's expansion, including recent pet food brand acquisitions, and aims to optimize its distribution network. The deal represents the largest industrial lease in the DFW region for 2024 so far.

summary: The Prevention through Design (PtD) Award, presented by NIOSH and partners, recognizes individuals, teams, and organizations for eliminating or reducing hazards through design efforts or contributing to the body of knowledge enabling PtD solutions. summary: Workers at an Apple store in Short Hills, New Jersey, have filed for union representation with the Communications Workers of America. This move is part of a broader unionization push across various companies in corporate America, including Starbucks, Amazon.com, and Microsoft, where employees are seeking better working conditions. Apple stated that it offers top-tier pay and comprehensive benefits to its retail teams.

summary: The article explores the significant impact of AI on cloud computing companies, noting that while AI has driven much of the equity market's recent gains, particularly for the "magnificent seven" tech companies, the broader economic benefits may take time to materialize. summary: Amazon.com Inc. has received approval to build a $73 million last-mile delivery station in Round Rock, an Austin suburb. title: Abbott Laboratories to close Bay Area site; almost 200 jobs to be cut
summary: Abbott Laboratories is closing its Fairfield, California location later this year, leading to the layoff of 195 employees. The company, known for brands like Similac and Pedialyte, attributed a decrease in its annual sales to an anticipated decline in COVID-19 testing-related sales, despite overall sales growth in the fourth quarter. Fairfield Mayor Cathrine Moy expressed frustration over the timing of the layoffs and the company's decision to discontinue the nutritional bar previously made at the plant.

title: Akamai expands cloud services with dedicated GPUs for media workloads
summary: Akamai Technologies Inc. has launched a new industry-optimized cloud service utilizing Nvidia RTX 4000 Ada generation GPUs, specifically designed for media workloads to enhance video encoding, decoding, and processing. This service aims to provide faster and more cost-effective solutions for media providers compared to standard virtual machines, leveraging Akamai's global edge network. Although optimized for media, the service is also capable of supporting other demanding tasks like generative AI training and inference.

title: Infinium and Kinetik Reach Innovative CO2 Utilization Agreement to Advance eFuels Production
summary: Infinium and Kinetik Holdings Inc. have formed a long-term agreement for Infinium to purchase captured carbon dioxide from Kinetik's Permian Basin operations. This CO2 will be used as a feedstock for Infinium's Project Roadrunner, which produces ultra-low carbon electrofuels (eFuels) including sustainable aviation fuel (eSAF), marking a new model for decarbonization in heavy transport and chemical industries. This partnership aims to significantly reduce lifecycle greenhouse gas emissions and repurpose waste CO2, showcasing a beneficial reuse solution within the energy sector.

title: Cloud Software Engineering Veteran Jeremy Ung Joins BlackLine as Chief Technology Officer
summary: BlackLine, a leader in digital finance transformation, has announced the appointment of Jeremy Ung as its new Chief Technology Officer, effective April 15. Ung, a cloud software engineering veteran with over 20 years of experience from companies like Apptio, Amazon Web Services, and Microsoft, will be responsible for guiding the technology direction of BlackLine's market-leading cloud platform. This strategic hire aims to enhance BlackLine's solutions through connected data and AI-powered platforms to meet the growing demand for automation and risk management in the Office of the CFO.

title: Cardinal Health breaks ground on 4th Ohio distribution center
summary: Cardinal Health has begun construction on a 350,000-square-foot logistics center in Columbus, Ohio, which will be its fourth distribution facility in the area. The new center, set to open by summer 2025, will be equipped with advanced automation technology from Honeywell Intelligrated to enhance inventory efficiency and product flow. This expansion aims to boost Cardinal Health's agility and responsiveness within its supply chain, particularly for its over-the-counter consumer business.

title: Amazon Prime Memberships in US Gain 8% to New High
summary: Amazon's Prime subscription service reached a new high of 180 million U.S. shoppers in March, an 8% increase from the previous year, according to Consumer Intelligence Research Partners. This growth indicates strong appeal for Amazon's fast delivery, despite inflation and increased online competition. Analysts project a 12% gain in Amazon's subscription services revenue for the period ended March 31.

title: UNFI refinances term loan with $500M agreement
summary: United Natural Foods Inc. (UNFI) is refinancing its senior secured term loan facility with a new $500 million agreement, following a debt downgrade by Moody's Ratings. The refinancing aims to extend the maturity date and modify interest rates, with proceeds used to repay the existing loan. Moody's cited UNFI's weak credit metrics and negative free cash flow for the downgrade but maintained a stable outlook, noting the company's strong position in the natural and organic food sector.

Morgan Chase & Co., Amazon, Wells Fargo, Deloitte, and PwC lead LinkedIn's 8th annual Top Companies list for 2024, highlighting 50 best large workplaces in the U.S. The list is compiled using LinkedIn data to measure career success based on promotion rates and skill development. This year's honorees are recognized for their investment in employee experience, including upskilling initiatives and flexible working arrangements.

title: JEPI: Do Not Make The Same Mistake Two Years In A Row, Buy This Covered Call ETF Instead
summary: The article compares the 2023 and Q1 2024 performance of three S&P 500 covered call ETFs: JEPI, XYLD, and SPYI, highlighting their total returns and tax efficiency. It argues that SPYI consistently outperformed its peers due to its strategy of writing out-of-the-money covered calls and favorable Section 1256 tax treatment. The author advises investors to choose SPYI for better price appreciation, income, and tax efficiency, particularly given the S&P 500's continued rally.

title: Cisco debuts new AI-focused security system after $28 billion deal to buy Splunk
summary: Cisco launched HyperShield, a new AI-focused security product, after its $28 billion acquisition of Splunk, aiming to protect applications, devices, and data across various IT environments. The technology is designed to address the challenges posed by new digital AI assistants like ChatGPT and improve vulnerability patching times from days to minutes. This move is part of Cisco's strategy to become a serious AI player and boost its cybersecurity business as it faces competition in its traditional market.

title: How to Find Cloud Software Company Stocks to Trade and Invest
summary: This article provides guidance on investing in cloud computing stocks, detailing different types of cloud services (IaaS, PaaS, SaaS) and key factors influencing stock performance like market demand and financial health. It offers investment strategies, including individual stocks (e.g., ServiceNow, Zoom) and ETFs (e.g., Global X Cloud Computing ETF), and lists major players like Amazon, Microsoft, and Adobe in the cloud software industry.

title: Hyperscale data center capacity to double every four years - report
summary: A new report by Synergy Research Group indicates that hyperscale data center capacity will double every four years for the next decade, driven primarily by demand for cloud services and AI tools. The number of active hyperscale facilities has surpassed 1,000 globally, with AI accelerating the scale of new data centers. The US accounts for 51 percent of worldwide capacity, while Amazon, Microsoft, and Google collectively represent 60 percent of all hyperscale data center capacity.

title: HanesBrands Announces Substantial Progress Toward Reaching Sustainability Goals Around People, Planet and Product
summary: HanesBrands Inc. announced significant progress toward its 2025/2030 sustainability goals in its 2023 Sustainability Summary Report, encompassing People, Planet, and Product pillars. The company has reduced greenhouse gas emissions by 53% since 2019 and aims for zero waste by 2025 and 100% renewable electricity by 2030. HanesBrands has also recognized substantial savings from its sustainability investments and advanced efforts to improve lives globally.

title: PCA’s corrugated product shipments rise as demand rebounds
summary: Packaging Corporation of America (PCA) saw corrugated product shipments rise in Q1 2024, exceeding expectations due to a rebound in demand across all sectors and the end of customer destocking. Despite positive volume trends, executives expressed frustration with Fastmarkets RISI’s pricing index not fully reflecting announced price increases. PCA also reopened paper machines earlier than planned and expects a Q2 financial impact from scheduled maintenance.

title: Amazon Introduces Low-Cost Grocery Delivery Subscription for Prime Members and Customers Using EBT
summary: Amazon has launched a new grocery delivery subscription in over 3,500 U.S. cities and towns. Prime members can subscribe for $9.99 per month, offering unlimited deliveries on orders over $35 from Whole Foods Market, Amazon Fresh, and other local retailers. Customers with EBT cards can access the same benefits for a discounted rate of $4.99 per month, with a free 30-day trial available.

title: Clean Energy Announces First Injection of Renewable Natural Gas at Victory Farms Dairy
summary: Clean Energy Fuels Corp. has announced the completion and successful injection of renewable natural gas (RNG) into the interstate natural gas infrastructure from its new facility at Victory Farms Dairy in Revillo, South Dakota. This facility, utilizing manure from 6,000 jersey cows, is expected to produce 900,000 gallons of negative carbon-intensity RNG annually, contributing to the decarbonization of heavy-duty transportation. The project, a partnership with Dynamic Renewables, aims to meet the growing demand for RNG and reduce greenhouse gas emissions.

title: 3 reasons the iShares S&P 500 ETF (IVV) is a great long-term investment
summary: The iShares S&P 500 ETF (IVV) is presented as an appealing long-term investment for Australians, despite the local ASX market. The article highlights three main reasons: its remarkably low management fees of 0.04%, its investment in 500 of the largest and most profitable US companies like Microsoft and Amazon, and its strong historical returns, averaging over 16% per annum over the last five and ten years.

title: Here’s a look at the world’s first civil space traffic coordination system
summary: The article discusses the development of the Traffic Coordination System for Space (TraCSS), the world's first civil space traffic coordination system. Managed by the U.S. Commerce Department's Office of Space Commerce (OSC) and running on AWS, this system aims to transfer U.S. space coordination from military to civil authority. The project emphasizes minimal government infrastructure and an agile acquisition process to define safety metrics without competing with commercial space situational awareness companies.

title: Hillwood Acquires 3-Building Office Portfolio in Irving
summary: Dallas-based developer Hillwood has acquired the Freeport Business Center, a three-building office portfolio in Irving, Texas. This Class-A complex spans 34 acres, offering over 383,000 rentable square feet and boasting a 70% occupancy rate with notable tenants like Northrop Grumman Corp. and Boeing. The acquisition is a strategic move by Hillwood to secure quality real estate in infill locations, capitalizing on recent capital improvements and its prime proximity to DFW International Airport and major highways.

title: Marathon Petroleum (MPC) Declares $0.825 Quarterly Dividend; 1.7% Yield
summary: Marathon Petroleum (MPC) has declared a quarterly dividend of $0.825 per share, totaling $3.3 annualized, resulting in an annual yield of 1.7 percent. The dividend is payable on June 10, 2024, to stockholders of record as of May 16, 2024, with an ex-dividend date of May 15, 2024.

title: Graham Holdings moving headquarters to trophy high-rise building in Rosslyn
summary: Graham Holdings, the company that previously owned The Washington Post, is relocating its corporate headquarters to a 35-story trophy building at 1812 N. Moore Street in Rosslyn, Virginia. The company has signed a 15-year lease for the entire 21st floor of the building, which also houses Nestle USA's headquarters. This move highlights the strong demand for Class A and top-tier office spaces in the D.C. area, despite high overall vacancy rates.

title: Amazon fined by Italian antitrust regulator
summary: Amazon has been fined €10 million by Italy’s antitrust regulator for engaging in unfair business practices. The regulator alleged that Amazon's automatic "Subscribe and Save" function significantly restricted consumers' freedom of choice by pre-setting recurring purchases. Amazon plans to appeal the decision, asserting that the program helps customers save money and time on regular deliveries.

title: 6 Questions For Adam Singolda, Founder & CEO, Taboola
summary: Adam Singolda, founder and CEO of Taboola, discusses the company's evolution from its inception in 2007 to its current position as a public company nearing $2 billion in revenue. title: Newegg creates free membership program, offering perks to participants
summary: Newegg has launched Newegg+, a free customer membership program offering perks such as free shipping, expedited returns, and exclusive deals. The electronics retailer aims to enhance the shopping experience and gather customer feedback to expand the program in the future. This initiative aligns with the growing trend of loyalty programs among Top 1000 retailers, which are used to gather data and drive customer behavior.

title: Microsoft Reports Rising Revenues as A.I. Investments Bear Fruit (Published 2024)
summary: Microsoft announced a 17% increase in revenue and a 20% rise in profit for the first three months of the year, driven significantly by its investments in artificial intelligence and strong growth in its cloud computing product, Azure. The company's A.I. services, particularly in generative A.I., contributed to a 31% growth in Azure sales and helped Microsoft gain market share from Amazon. Microsoft also saw substantial growth in its gaming division, boosted by the acquisition of Activision Blizzard, and better-than-expected performance in Windows software sales as the PC market stabilized.

title: Focus: UPS, FedEx transition to electric vans slowed by battery shortages, low supply
summary: UPS and FedEx are facing significant hurdles in electrifying their delivery fleets due to battery shortages, high EV prices, and the failure of some electric van manufacturers. This transition is crucial for President Biden's climate goals, but the companies also face reduced access to California's EV purchase vouchers, further complicating their efforts to replace gas-guzzling vehicles. Despite these challenges, both companies are exploring alternative fuel options and continuing their electrification plans.

title: Alphabet issues first-ever dividend, $70 billion buyback
summary: Alphabet announced its first-ever dividend of 20 cents per share and a new $70 billion share repurchase program. This news, released alongside better-than-expected first-quarter earnings, drove the Google parent's shares up 15%. Alphabet's move follows Meta's initiation of a dividend, indicating a trend of increased maturity signals from large-cap tech companies.

title: HRH the Hereditary Grand Duke and Xavier Bettel on a working visit to the United States
summary: HRH the Hereditary Grand Duke and Minister for Foreign Affairs and Foreign Trade, Xavier Bettel, conducted a working visit to the United States, including Detroit, Cleveland, New York, and Delaware, to deepen relations with American industrial investors in Luxembourg. The visit focused on the space economy, with Minister Bettel emphasizing cooperation and sustainability in space, and culminated in the 11th Luxembourg-American Business Award being presented to Redwire for its contributions to the space industry. The delegation also met with executives from Redwire, AIAC, and DuPont.

summary: Alphabet Inc., Google's parent company, announced its first-ever cash dividend of 20 cents per share and a new $70 billion stock repurchase program following strong Q1 2024 earnings. CEO Sundar Pichai highlighted robust performance from Search, YouTube, and Cloud, attributing success to the "Gemini era" and AI leadership. This move, similar to Meta's recent dividend, signals tech industry maturity and has been positively received by investors.

title: Creativity and innovation drive Chinese animation industry
summary: The Chinese animation industry is experiencing significant growth, driven by creative content and technological advancements, with a total output value of 300 billion yuan (US$41.5 billion). Platforms like Bilibili, Tencent, and iQiyi are investing heavily in original content, targeting younger audiences, and leveraging AI to enhance production quality. Chinese animated films, often inspired by traditional culture, are gaining international recognition and competing with foreign blockbusters.

title: Upgrade your Steam Deck storage with Corsair's MP600 Mini 1TB SSD for just £70
summary: Amazon UK is offering the 1TB Corsair MP600 Mini SSD for £69.98, a significant saving for Steam Deck owners looking to expand their storage. This compact M.2 2230 SSD provides faster loading times, though the Steam Deck itself is limited to PCIe 3.0 speeds. For those needing even more space, a 2TB variant is available, or users can opt for a cheaper microSD card upgrade.

summary: The Netgear Orbi 970 is reviewed as a very fast but expensive Wi-Fi 7 mesh system, offering phenomenal speeds over Wi-Fi 6 and multiple multi-gigabit Ethernet ports. title: CEOs of Microsoft, Nvidia and other tech giants join federal AI advisory board
summary: A federal AI advisory board has been established, comprising prominent tech executives, academics, and civil rights leaders, including CEOs from Microsoft, Nvidia, and OpenAI. Led by Secretary of Homeland Security Alejandro Mayorkas, the board will advise the Department of Homeland Security on the safe application of AI in critical infrastructure and issue recommendations for organizations like power grid operators and manufacturers. This initiative stems from President Biden's executive order on AI, which also mandates data sharing on new AI models' safety with the government.

title: Biz Buzz: Office Depot to depart from Galveston; Chipotle crews are busy on Stewart Road
summary: Office Depot is closing its Galveston location at 2711 61st St. as part of a larger corporate strategy to analyze store profitability and shift focus, potentially towards online presence or more profitable regions. Meanwhile, Chipotle Mexican Grill is moving ahead with its plans for an island restaurant at 6229 Stewart Road, with crews beginning work on the former Capital One building for a projected summer opening. This column also promises more business opening news next week.

title: Why I Just Added This Ultra-High-Yield Dividend ETF to My Retirement Account
summary: The author recently added the JPMorgan Nasdaq Equity Premium Income ETF (JEPQ) to their retirement account, aiming for consistent passive income and price appreciation with lower volatility. JEPQ offers a high dividend yield (9.2% over 30 days, 10.8% over 12 months) through a strategy of holding a high-quality equity portfolio and selling out-of-the-money call options on the Nasdaq-100 index. This approach is designed to generate monthly income and provide relatively steady returns, making it an attractive investment for retirement planning.

title: Forget Individual Consumer Stocks: Buy This ETF Instead
summary: The article suggests that instead of investing in individual consumer discretionary stocks, investors should consider the VanEck Retail ETF (RTH). This ETF focuses on the U.S. consumer discretionary sector with a concentrated portfolio of 26 holdings, led by Amazon. The RTH ETF has demonstrated outperformance compared to its competitors and the S&P 500 over the past five years, justifying its slightly higher expense ratio.

title: Fox’s New Ad-Sales Chief Will Tout Tom Brady, Super Bowl LIX in TV Upfront
summary: Fox's new ad-sales chief, Jeff Collins, plans to leverage the upcoming Super Bowl LIX broadcast and Tom Brady's debut as an NFL announcer to attract advertisers during the annual TV upfront market. Collins emphasizes Fox's strategy of focusing on being "best in class" and offering distinct audiences across its diverse media portfolio, including broadcast, sports, Fox News, and Tubi, to counter market pressures from streaming services. He anticipates strong demand for Super Bowl LIX ad slots, despite increasing competition in the advertising landscape.

title: How to Buy Roku Stock Online in 2021
summary: This guide explains how to invest in Roku stock, detailing the company's background, growth potential, and current financial standing. It outlines a three-step process for buying Roku shares through online brokers like eToro, emphasizing reasons to consider the investment such as global expansion, increasing ad revenue, and a healthy balance sheet. The article also touches upon risks, market competition, and analyst outlooks for Roku.

title: How to Buy Alphabet (Google) Stock Online in 2025
summary: This article provides a comprehensive guide on how to buy Alphabet (Google) stock online in 2025, detailing steps, top brokers, and reasons to invest in the company. It covers Google's diverse services, its financial performance, business strategy, and historical stock information, emphasizing its growth and expansion into new technologies like AI. The article also addresses common FAQs regarding Alphabet stock.

title: Over the past decade, C.H. Robinson lost its moat to innovation and competition
summary: C.H. Robinson, once the uncontested leader in trucking freight brokerage, has seen its competitive advantages eroded due to intense innovation and competition. Despite reporting strong results during the COVID-19 pandemic, the company is now struggling with declining market share and internal employee dissatisfaction due to compensation changes. The article suggests that a significant business model reset is necessary for C.H. Robinson to navigate the evolving market and satisfy investor expectations.

title: After Earnings, Is Meta Stock a Buy, a Sell, or Fairly Valued?
summary: Morningstar assessed Meta Platforms' stock following its Q1 earnings report, maintaining a "Wide" economic moat rating but deeming the stock overvalued with a 2-star rating and a $400 fair value estimate. The article highlights Meta's strong core advertising business, driven by AI investments, but also points out the high uncertainty due to speculative AI initiatives and competition. Investors are advised to be comfortable with Meta's aggressive investment in new technologies, as regulatory risks and dependence on online advertising remain significant concerns.

title: Ingles, a dynasty: Founding family still in control
summary: Ingles Markets, a publicly traded regional grocer, remains firmly under the control of its founding family, specifically Robert "Bobby" Ingle II, who holds 72 percent of the voting power. This control allows him significant influence over company decisions, including his own compensation and land deals with his private companies. Despite challenges from competitors and concerns from outside stockholders about corporate structure and property management, the company remains family-run with no immediate plans for succession, and Bobby Ingle continues to assert his control over the company's future.

title: Amazon’s stock inches up as cost-cutting measures and AI investment boost AWS profits
summary: Amazon's stock increased after reporting better-than-expected first-quarter earnings, driven by strong performance in its cloud computing unit, Amazon Web Services (AWS), and its advertising business. The company's profitability soared due to extensive cost-cutting measures and significant investments in AI, particularly in AWS, which has now become a $100 billion annual business. Despite these successes, Amazon remains the only trillion-dollar market cap internet company not to issue a dividend.

title: As You Sow Calls Out Big Tech for $5 Billion Loss in 401(k) Returns
summary: A report by the non-profit As You Sow and researchers at the University of Waterloo indicates that over two million employees of 12 tech companies missed out on $5.1 billion in retirement savings. This loss is attributed to the companies' 401(k) plans not adopting sustainable investing strategies, specifically by retaining investments in fossil fuels. The study found a significant difference in 10-year returns for portfolios without fossil fuels, leading As You Sow to accuse these companies of greenwashing and urge them to offer sustainable investment options.

title: TV Shopping Networks Aren't Doing Great — So QVC And HSN Are Merging
summary: Retail giants QVC and HSN are merging, with QVC acquiring HSN for $2.1 billion, to combat declining sales and stay competitive against online retailers like Amazon and Walmart. Despite the merger, both QVC and HSN will continue to operate as separate brands, leveraging combined resources in the challenging online shopping era. Their struggle highlights how even established home-shopping networks are impacted by the shift towards e-commerce, as evidenced by Amazon's previous attempt at a shopping show with "Style Code Live" which was canceled after a year.

title: Why Is Marin Software (MRIN) Stock Up 23% Today?
summary: Marin Software (MRIN) stock surged 23% today following the announcement of its new AI-powered Anomaly Detector. This tool helps businesses identify unusual data across various ad platforms like Google, Meta, and Amazon, enabling them to quickly act on opportunities or issues. The news has led to exceptionally heavy trading volume for MRIN shares.

title: Amazon sales surge as company trains focus on artificial intelligence
summary: Amazon reported record first-quarter sales, with revenue rising 13% to $143.3 billion and profit surging to $10.4 billion, exceeding Wall Street expectations. This growth was largely driven by a renewed focus on artificial intelligence, particularly in its cloud-computing unit, Amazon Web Services (AWS), which saw sales increase over 17%. CEO Andy Jassy highlighted AI as a critical building block for Amazon's future growth, aiming to generate "tens of billions of dollars" of revenue from it in the coming years.
